Name: [P3] PF-RNG: Proposal of Entropy Collection Model for Wireless Secure Communication Channel of Ultra Low-Cost Computing Device
Description: Proposed a lightweight entropy collection model for secure wireless communication in ultra-low-cost computing environments.  The approach uses COTS wireless communication modules and parity feedback to assess the reliability of collected entropy while maintaining low hardware complexity and cost.

Name: [P2] Study on packet extraction before encryption with SSL
Publisher: Conference on Information Security and Cryptography 2018 Winter (CISC-W 2018)

Name: [P4] Automated Building Fuzzing Environment using Test Framework
Description: Proposed an automated approach for generating fuzzing environments for library testing using existing test frameworks.  The system automatically generates fuzzing executables and seed corpora by analyzing test code, reducing the manual effort required to prepare library fuzzing environments.
Publisher: Journal of the Korea Institute of Information Security & Cryptology

Name: [P5] A Fuzzing Seed Generation Technique Using Natural Language Processing Model
Description: Developed DDRFuzz, a fuzzing seed generation system based on sequence-to-sequence models.  The approach automatically generates high-quality seed files for fuzzing multimedia applications and was evaluated against existing seed generation techniques across five open-source applications.
Publisher: Journal of the Korea Institute of Information Security & Cryptology

Name: [P6] Automatically Seed Corpus and Fuzzing Executables Generation Using Test Framework
Description: Developed FuzzBuilderEx, an automated fuzzing environment generation system for library fuzzing.  The system performs static and dynamic analysis of test code to automatically generate fuzzing executables and seed corpora compatible with existing fuzzers such as AFL.  Evaluated the approach on nine open-source libraries, achieving a 31.2% increase in code coverage and detecting 58.7% more unique crashes compared with previous studies. The research also identified three zero-day vulnerabilities, including one registered as a CVE.

Name: [P7] Infotainment System Matters: Understanding the Impact and Implications of In-Vehicle Infotainment System Hacking with Automotive Grade Linux
Description: Research on the security impact of Automotive Grade Linux (AGL)-based in-vehicle infotainment systems through Cyber Security Challenge 2021.  Analyzed 33 verified proof-of-concept exploits targeting 11 AGL components and investigated their impact, including data leakage, system manipulation, denial of service, and lateral movement to connected systems.  Received the Best Paper Award at ACM CODASPY 2023.
Publisher: In Proceedings of the Thirteenth ACM Conference on Data and Application Security and Privacy (CODASPY '23)
